CA_dairy.label: Canadian dairy quota (supply management)

q43.N: MSQ numeric cap set by CMSMC since 1970 (+ tariff-rate import quotas)
q43.G: provincial board quota registries & quota exchanges
q43.W: Farm Products Agencies Act 1972; CDC (1966); federal-provincial boards; USMCA/CPTPP kept SM 'fundamentally intact'
q43.P: MSQ CAD 25,000 -> 30,000 per kg butterfat; total quota value CAD 35 bln (2018)

observed: CMSMC sets national Market Sharing Quota since 1970; provincial boards allocate and sanction (Wikipedia: Dairy and poultry supply management in Canada)

USMCA (01.10.2018): supply management 'remained fundamentally intact' with milk-class concessions

LHR_slots.label: London Heathrow slots (IATA WSG regime)

q43.S: scarce takeoff/landing capacity at Level-3 airport
q43.N: WSG 80/20 use-it-or-lose-it + UK slot regulations (Level 3 coordination)
q43.G: slot coordinator registries (Airport Coordination Ltd/WWACG databases)
q43.W: Worldwide Airport Slot Board (IATA+ACI+WWACG); UK DfT/Parliament waiver legislation
q43.P: USD 52.3m/pair (Continental, 2008); USD 75m/pair (Oman Air, 2016); USD 27m single slot (Air NZ, 03.2020); 'record $75M' (Simple Flying, 08.2025)
q43.M: grandfathering: historic precedent = free first allocation

observed: 80/20 rule and waiver practice documented; COVID-19 listed among waiver episodes (Wikipedia: Airport slot)
IATA called for suspension of 80:20 as coronavirus crisis widened (The Loadstar, 02.03.2020)

UK government legislated slot waiver extension from 26.03.2021: airlines do not have to fly 80% to retain slots, 'acting on calls for relief from the aviation sector' (GOV.UK, DfT, 26.02.2021) -> D2 political donor acted, places kept at no cost
mechanism survived COVID: slots still trade at record values (Simple Flying 28.08.2025: Heathrow slots hit record $75M; Reuters 09.11.2021: Gatwick/Wizz urge reinstatement of rules)
Air NZ sold a Heathrow slot for USD 27m in distress (Forbes, 06.03.2020): place separable, mechanism intact, holder changed
